items.q: Systematic sampling may be defined as

selection at a fixed interval through an ordered list after a random starting point
the extent to which findings from the people studied apply to a wider group
methods that summarise the features of a set of observations without reaching beyond them

Type I error

the application of statistical reasoning to questions about health, disease and care
the number of new cases arising in a group over a stated period
a characteristic that can take only whole counts, such as the number of children born

distortion in which people with an outcome remember past exposures differently from those without it
the extent to which findings from the people studied apply to a wider group

a characteristic that can take only whole counts, such as the number of children born
facts already collected for another purpose and reused to answer a new question
